INDEPENDENT · UNOFFICIAL FIELD GUIDE

How to play Azeroth Survivors

Last updated: October 29, 2026

Field guide

What is Azeroth Survivors?How to playBuildsTier listDownload & fixesSafety checkTalent treeLuck

Step 1 — Open the maintained entry point.

Go to Aethus's own site. Use a current Chrome or Edge on a desktop or laptop. If the loader says your browser has no WebGPU, update the browser first, then enable hardware/GPU acceleration. Click inside the game canvas before you try any key; without focus, keyboard input will not register.

Step 2 — Pick a class, not a "best" class.

For a first clear, Warrior or Paladin. Warrior has the largest health pool and a Whirlwind capstone that turns into blender mode; Paladin brings Consecration, shields, self-heal and a once-per-90-second death save. Both forgive positioning mistakes while your talent rows are still locked. Hunter, Warlock and Mage have higher power ceilings, but they ask you to know enemy movement before they pay off.

Step 3 — Minutes 0–3: take wave-clear only.

Your first six levels are about turning the spawn curve into experience. Take area spells — Blizzard, Volley, Consecration, Rain of Fire, Chain Lightning. If you started a single-target class, your first area tool has to be online before the first boss at around 2:15.

Step 4 — Minutes 3–8: commit to one carry.

Push your best area spell toward rank 8 and add exactly one survival tool — a slow, a stun, or a movement passive. The mobility spell lands around this window. Spend your three rerolls here, in the level 6–12 range, because a bad hand at this point costs the most tempo.

Step 5 — Minutes 8–15: rank-ups only.

Your slots are full. Every card is now a stat line: damage % on the carry first, cooldown % second, survival last. Bosses resist control at this stage — burst windows beat CC chains.

Step 6 — Between runs.

Check Collection, Armory and Talents before you queue again. Boss gear is permanent for that class, and the armory is where you see what your class can actually find.

First-run checklist

Common first-run mistakes

  • Reloading during first load.
  • Playing on a laptop trackpad without clicking the canvas.
  • Taking single-target cards before an area tool.
  • Spending rerolls in the first three levels.
